statements.t: We do not expect meaningful revenue, if any, during the aircraft development phase.

R&D expenses were $48.3 million in 3Q26 compared to $44.9 million in 3Q25 and reflect increasing supplier engagement and R&D activities – including eVTOL development and allocation of Embraer engineering resources to our project.

In the first nine months of 2026, Eve’s cash consumption reached $173.1 million and full year 2026 cashflow consumption is now expected to reach the low-end of our guidance of $225/275 million as Eve continues to capture synergies with Embraer.
The prototype is representative of Eve 100, our aircraft; it features similar systems and the same Lift + Cruise configuration that will be present in our commercial aircraft.
As mentioned previously, we will use one of Embraer’s hangars in São José dos Campos to assemble all the prototypes we plan to launch for the certification campaign.
With the expected completion of all the CRD processes by the end of 2026, we will continue to receive additional tolling and components that are necessary for the assembly of our prototypes.
We plan to build up to six prototypes with all the redundancies, systems and physical characteristics that will be featured in the commercial versions of our aircraft.
These will be extensively tested and used to accumulate hours to be counted towards our certification campaign.
We expect the first flight of our first conforming prototype in the second half of 2027.
The eighth lifter of our conforming prototype is now undergoing the last battery of tests, after many successful completed tests, which confirmed they are all on track for delivery/assembly.

Importantly, because the certification protocol allows ground tests (with the aid of rigs, high-fidelity simulations, our Iron Bird, and other ground equipment) to earn certification credits, our certification campaign will begin before the initial flights of the certification-compliant prototypes.
We expect to initiate EASA certification tests in mid-2028 and certification process to last ~18 months.

Total Cash Consumption Between $225 and $275 Million With intensifying program development efforts, increased engagement with suppliers, and initial assembly of our certification prototypes, Eve expects to consume between $225 million and $275 million in 2026.
We will also acquire raw materials and parts for certification-conforming prototypes.
We expect our investments and expenses to stay high in the upcoming quarters, mainly due to strong engineering engagement and possible supplier payments.
With $173.1 million consumed in the first nine months of the year, cash use for the full year is leaning towards the low-end our expected cash-consumption goals.
